title: x_lobstack receipt
description:
The Lobstack Gateway receipt: what a request cost, what served it, and what any reported saving was measured against.

WHERE IT APPEARS. On a streamed response (`stream: true`) this object is the `x_lobstack` member of the FINAL `chat.completion.chunk` — the frame with an empty `choices` array that also carries `usage`, sent after the chunk carrying `finish_reason` and before `data: [DONE]`. On a buffered response the same facts are carried in `x-lobstack-*` response headers instead, because a buffered response has nowhere else to put them; the header spellings are given in `x-header` on each property below. There is no third transport.

WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM `usage`. `usage` keeps the exact OpenAI shape so that a client which has never heard of Lobstack parses it unchanged. Everything Lobstack-specific hangs off `x_lobstack`, which such a client ignores.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY. Members not described here MAY be added. A client MUST ignore members it does not recognise, and MUST NOT treat their presence as an error.

request_id.description: The id of the trace row for this request, also returned as the `x-lobstack-request-id` response header and as `error.request_id` on a failure. It is allocated before anything can fail, so even a rejected request has one. Quoting it identifies the request exactly.

served_model.description: The model key that actually served the request. A client MUST NOT assume this equals the model it asked for: a named model is a ceiling, not a command, and the router may serve something cheaper.

requested_model.description: What the caller asked for: a model key, or the literal string `auto`. On a buffered response this has no header — the caller's own request is the only record of it.

routed.description: True when `requested_model` was `auto`, and true when the served model differs from the one the caller named.

cost_usd.description:
WHAT THE CALLER OWES for these tokens, in USD, priced at the moment the request was served.

`null` means UNPRICED: the served model is not in the price registry, or the request was never metered (a stream that failed before metering, for instance). `null` does NOT mean free and does NOT mean zero.

A client MUST NOT render `null` as `0`, `$0.00`, or any other currency amount, and MUST NOT substitute a default. It MUST either render the value as unknown or omit the figure. Clients MUST NOT compute this figure themselves by multiplying token counts against a local copy of the rate card: a local copy drifts from the catalogue, and a model it does not know silently prices at zero.

On a buffered response the header carries an EMPTY STRING where this member is `null`. `Number("")` is `0`, so parsers MUST test for the empty string before converting.

savings_usd.description:
`baseline_cost_usd` minus `cost_usd`: what these exact token counts would have cost on the baseline model, minus what they actually cost. `null` when there is no baseline, and therefore no honest subtraction to report.

A client MUST NOT render this figure without also rendering `baseline_reason`, because the two reasons are different claims. See `baseline_reason`.

priced.description: False when the request could not be priced, in which case `cost_usd` is `null`. True when it was priced, in which case `cost_usd` is a number. It exists so a client can tell "we could not price this" apart from any other reason a figure might be missing.

baseline_model.description: The model `savings_usd` was measured against. `null` exactly when `baseline_reason` is `null`.

baseline_reason.description:
Why `baseline_model` is the comparison, and therefore what `savings_usd` means. The two non-null values are NOT interchangeable and a client MUST NOT present them identically.

`named` — the caller asked for `baseline_model` and the Gateway served something else. The comparison is like-for-like against the caller's own request, and `savings_usd` is a measurement. This is the only value for which a client MAY use unqualified language such as "saved".

`plan_ceiling` — the caller sent `auto` and named nothing. `baseline_model` is the most expensive model the caller's plan may reach: what they would have paid had they asked for the best one. It is a real subtraction between two real prices, and it is also the most flattering number available to the seller, and the caller never asked for that model. A client MUST label such a figure as a comparison against a plan ceiling, and MUST NOT present it as a saving against what the caller requested.

`null` — there is no honest comparison, and `savings_usd`, `baseline_model` and `baseline_cost_usd` are all `null`. This occurs when the caller named the model that was served (nothing was routed away from), when either model cannot be priced, and when an `auto` request comes from a plan with no defined ceiling.

baseline_cost_usd.description: What `baseline_model` would have charged for these exact token counts, priced on the same basis as `cost_usd` so that the subtraction is between two comparable numbers. `null` exactly when `baseline_reason` is `null`.

allOf.$comment: priced and cost_usd agree in both directions: priced true implies a number, priced false implies null. A client that trusts one need not re-derive the other.
The three baseline members travel together. A reason implies both a model and a priced baseline; no reason implies all three are null, and no saving is reported.
